corpus: v29-02-s6h (harder set; the 2026-10-23 set in ../frozen.json stays as it was)
why: the 2026-10-23 set scored blind attribution 60/60 in both arms (gain 0, at the ceiling); owner decision 2026-10-25 item 12: Sol writes a harder card set; floors unchanged
author: opencode openai/gpt-6.1-sol (run --standalone, tools-off agent), one call, prompt sol-prompt.md; output used unedited
harderBecause: Role, age, pronouns, rank, personality, available information, scenario, and opening message are matched; unlike the previous set, none supplies a speaker-specific motive, relationship, or life history.
The only differing card details are hair and eye colour, and no situation invokes them; the situations instead give all three clerks the same workplace evidence and the same opportunity to respond.

The sheets distinguish syntax, register, and rhythm rather than subject matter: fragments and direct openings, balanced formal clauses, or conversational linked clauses. Attribution must therefore depend on wording rather than a distinctive task or anecdote.

With sheets off, the prospective prediction is substantially lower attribution than the previous ceiling, potentially near the three-speaker chance level, because the underlying cards provide no systematic voice distinction.

If prevention works, the prospective prediction is an attribution gain of at least 10 percentage points and at least 25 percent fewer combined avoid-and-tic hits per reply; the compact sheets keep each rendered guidance line below 120 tokens under the specified character-based estimate.

If prevention does not work, the prospective prediction is little or no attribution gain and no reliable targeted-repetition reduction; continued ceiling attribution in both arms would instead indicate that this set still fails to remove attribution shortcuts.

design.cardsDifferOnlyIn: hair and eye colour (same role, age, rank, personality, scenario, first_mes; mes_example empty)
design.replyOrder: rotates per situation (s1: Brelan, Nerik, Veska; s2: Nerik, Veska, Brelan; ...)
design.narrator: DM Narrator posts each situation with /sendas (not generated)
design.guidanceEstimateTokens: about 85-95 per member (chars/4 of the rendered line), under the 120 floor before measurement

arms.baseline: characters.delivery off (ext_setting, restored by the runner)

stopRules.zeroTolerance: none in this row (leak floor is the jest/payload half)
stopRules.blindMetric: attribution is paired and blind: no S4 early pass; every situation runs
stopRules.S5: a harness error or backend outage stops the row as NOT A MEASUREMENT after one retry
stopRules.pairs: arms are separate chats run back to back (the 2026-10-23 protocol), not interleaved per item; the scorer counts only situations complete in both arms, so a stop leaves balanced pairs

rater: rate.mjs: opencode openai/gpt-6.1-sol, names (members, DM Narrator, player names passed as args) replaced by [name], 120 replies shuffled blind to arm (seed 20261025), member list with each sheet notes, unclear = wrong; second call re-rates 10 prevention replies for self-agreement
repetition: per reply: authored tic + avoid hits (case-insensitive whole phrase) for the speaker
guidance: from the prevention arm payload capture (st-payload arm --persist): delivery line chars/4 per drafted request; report n, max, p95
